symptom: Guest kernel panic on boot with 'VFS: Cannot open root device vda or unknown-block(0,0)'. vmlinux size jumped from ~29MB to ~38MB after upgrading to a 6.1 build.
error_patterns: Kernel panic - not syncing: VFS: Unable to mount root fs

diagnostic_steps.action: Capture guest kernel panic via serial console
diagnostic_steps.command: Add console=ttyS0 to boot_args; PUT /serial; reproduce
diagnostic_steps.expected: VFS panic message in console output

diagnostic_steps.action: Verify guest kernel build size and configs
diagnostic_steps.expected: All required configs =y; size sane vs prior build

diagnostic_steps.action: Compare against Firecracker reference guest configs
diagnostic_steps.expected: Spot the missing CONFIG entries

fix_steps.action: Rebuild guest kernel with the Firecracker reference config from resources/guest_configs/
If using Amazon Linux microvm-kernel, pin to a tagged release
fix_steps.validation: Tagged build matches Firecracker support matrix

symptom: MicroVM crashes immediately on InstanceStart with KVM_EXIT_FAIL_ENTRY when running Firecracker inside another VM (Azure VM, GCP VM, nested KVM).

diagnostic_steps.action: Confirm host is itself virtualized
diagnostic_steps.expected: If 'kvm' or 'microsoft' or 'amazon' returned → nested env

diagnostic_steps.action: Check KVM exit reason in Firecracker logs
diagnostic_steps.expected: Exit reason logged with cpu and hardware_entry_failure_reason

fix_steps.action: Move Firecracker to a bare-metal host (or .metal EC2 instance type)
If bare metal not available, use AWS C8i/M8i/R8i which support nested KVM (~10% perf tax)
fix_steps.command: Provision a Nitro instance with nested-virt support

symptom: VM hangs after 'random: crng init done' with no exception or message on AMD Zen processors (Zen, Zen+, Zen 2).

diagnostic_steps.action: Identify host CPU vendor and family
diagnostic_steps.expected: AuthenticAMD with Zen family

diagnostic_steps.action: Capture serial console past 'crng init done'
diagnostic_steps.command: Add console=ttyS0 to boot_args; capture full boot log
diagnostic_steps.expected: Output stops with no kernel oops

fix_steps.action: Apply CPU template that masks the problematic MSR exposure
fix_steps.command: PUT /cpu-config with template that filters MSR 0x10a (AMD platform-specific)
fix_steps.validation: VM boots past the freeze point
fix_steps.rollback: Boot without template — accept the freeze

fix_steps.action: Move workload to non-Zen AMD or Intel host
fix_steps.command: Re-host to EPYC Milan+ or Intel Ice Lake+

symptom: Firecracker exits at startup with 'Error creating Kvm object: Error(13)' (errno 13 = EACCES, permission denied).

diagnostic_steps.action: Check /dev/kvm permissions and group
diagnostic_steps.expected: crw-rw---- root:kvm; running uid should be in kvm group

diagnostic_steps.action: Confirm calling uid has access
diagnostic_steps.command: sudo -u <uid> test -r /dev/kvm && test -w /dev/kvm && echo OK || echo NO_ACCESS
diagnostic_steps.expected: OK

diagnostic_steps.action: Verify KVM kernel modules loaded
diagnostic_steps.expected: kvm and kvm_intel/kvm_amd present

fix_steps.action: Add the running uid to the kvm group
fix_steps.command: sudo usermod -aG kvm <user>; logout/login or newgrp kvm
fix_steps.validation: Re-run Firecracker; KVM object creates successfully

fix_steps.action: If running under jailer, ensure --uid/--gid maps to kvm-group-membered identity

symptom: Firecracker fails to start with 'Resource busy' on /dev/kvm. Another hypervisor (VMware Workstation, VirtualBox) is loaded and holds /dev/kvm exclusively.

diagnostic_steps.action: List loaded virt kernel modules
diagnostic_steps.expected: vboxdrv or vmmon present alongside kvm

diagnostic_steps.action: Check who has /dev/kvm open
diagnostic_steps.expected: VMware/VirtualBox process holds the fd

fix_steps.action: Unload conflicting hypervisor module
fix_steps.validation: lsof /dev/kvm shows no holder; Firecracker starts

fix_steps.action: Disable VirtualBox/VMware autostart

symptom: Host dmesg shows 'fc_vmm: page allocation failure: order:6, mode:0x140c0c0' during high-rate microVM creation. KVM cannot allocate large contiguous pages because host memory is fragmented.

diagnostic_steps.action: Confirm fragmentation state
diagnostic_steps.expected: Few or zero high-order free pages

diagnostic_steps.action: Check current vm.min_free_kbytes
diagnostic_steps.expected: If <128 MiB on a busy host, likely too low

fix_steps.action: Raise vm.min_free_kbytes to keep more reserve
fix_steps.command: sudo sysctl -w vm.min_free_kbytes=262144; echo 'vm.min_free_kbytes=262144' | sudo tee -a /etc/sysctl.conf
fix_steps.validation: Subsequent microVM creates succeed; buddyinfo shows higher-order pages

fix_steps.action: Trigger explicit memory compaction
If chronic, switch to hugepages-backed RAM (vm.nr_hugepages reserved + machine-config.huge_pages=2M)
fix_steps.validation: fc_vmm allocates from pre-reserved hugepages — no fragmentation
fix_steps.rollback: sysctl -w vm.nr_hugepages=0; remove huge_pages from machine-config

symptom: Firecracker process exits immediately with exit code 12 (Out of memory). Host cannot satisfy the requested guest memory size (default 128 MiB if /machine-config not set).

diagnostic_steps.action: Check exit code and /proc/meminfo at time of failure
diagnostic_steps.expected: Exit 12; MemFree very low

diagnostic_steps.action: Check for related dmesg page allocation failures
diagnostic_steps.command: sudo dmesg | grep -E 'page allocation|Out of memory|oom-killer'
diagnostic_steps.expected: Either page-alloc failures or OOM-killer events

fix_steps.action: Reduce machine-config.mem_size_mib or free host memory
fix_steps.command: PUT /machine-config {mem_size_mib: <smaller>}; or kill unrelated host processes

fix_steps.action: If chronic, raise vm.min_free_kbytes (see page-allocation-failure-fragmentation)

symptom: Guest with 16 GiB allocation OOM-killed despite host showing 9 GiB RSS / 64 GiB total. Memory accounting or page cache accumulation during heavy compilation workloads.

diagnostic_steps.action: Inspect cgroup memory accounting at OOM time
diagnostic_steps.expected: current near max; events.oom > 0

diagnostic_steps.action: Check guest page-cache pressure
diagnostic_steps.expected: Cached very high relative to MemFree

fix_steps.action: Attach a balloon device with deflate_on_oom for safety
fix_steps.validation: Future OOMs auto-deflate balloon (only helps if balloon was inflated)

fix_steps.action: Raise cgroup memory.max above mem_size_mib + overhead headroom
fix_steps.validation: Guest no longer OOM-killed at workload peak

fix_steps.action: Drop guest page cache periodically if unavoidable

symptom: Occasional KVM_EXIT_SHUTDOWN with 'bad system call (14)' (rt_sigprocmask) during VM shutdown — ~0-3 failures per 100 VMs.

diagnostic_steps.action: Capture audit log of seccomp violations
diagnostic_steps.command: sudo auditctl -a always,exit -F arch=b64 -S all -F key=fc-seccomp; reproduce; ausearch -k fc-seccomp
diagnostic_steps.expected: audit lines with syscall=14 (rt_sigprocmask)

diagnostic_steps.action: Confirm Firecracker version (was fixed in PR #1603)
diagnostic_steps.expected: Version that includes the fix

fix_steps.action: Upgrade to a Firecracker release that includes PR #1603
fix_steps.command: Update package or rebuild from main

symptom: Firecracker process exits with seccomp violation when receiving SIGSEGV/SIGBUS — Rust signal handler calls unwhitelisted sigaction syscall.

diagnostic_steps.action: Capture seccomp audit log around the crash
diagnostic_steps.expected: syscall=sigaction (or rt_sigaction) blocked

fix_steps.action: Upgrade to Firecracker version where sigaction is whitelisted in default filter
fix_steps.validation: SIGSEGV produces clean abort with handler output

fix_steps.action: Workaround: provide a custom seccomp filter that whitelists rt_sigaction

symptom: Firecracker panic produces a secondary seccomp violation — the panic handler calls mremap (Rust unwinding) which isn't in the default filter. Original panic info is lost.

diagnostic_steps.action: Locate the panic in logs (panic message comes BEFORE the seccomp kill)
diagnostic_steps.expected: Original panic message visible above the seccomp line

fix_steps.action: Upgrade Firecracker to version with mremap in default seccomp filter
fix_steps.validation: Panic produces full backtrace before exit

symptom: Firecracker thread becomes unresponsive after receiving a signal (SIGSEGV/SIGSYS). Custom signal handlers write logs and flush metrics — these use locks for synchronization but are NOT async-signal-safe. Handler intercepts signal on a thread already holding the lock → deadlock.
error_patterns: no further log output after signal

diagnostic_steps.action: Detect unresponsive Firecracker via API ping
diagnostic_steps.expected: Timeout / no response

diagnostic_steps.action: Inspect thread state to confirm deadlock
diagnostic_steps.expected: Thread blocked on log/metrics mutex inside signal handler

fix_steps.action: Run an overwatcher that SIGKILLs unresponsive Firecracker processes
fix_steps.command: Periodic loop: ping API; if no response within timeout → kill -9 <pid>

symptom: Guest `poweroff` shuts down the OS but the Firecracker process stays alive — no ACPI PM means there's no way for the guest to signal poweroff to the VMM.
error_patterns: guest powered off but firecracker process still running

diagnostic_steps.action: Confirm guest is x86_64 (ARM has PSCI and works correctly)
diagnostic_steps.expected: x86_64 → expected behavior; aarch64 → file separate issue

diagnostic_steps.action: Verify Firecracker process state
diagnostic_steps.expected: Process running, vCPU thread idle in KVM_RUN

fix_steps.action: Use SendCtrlAltDel API action instead of guest poweroff
fix_steps.rollback: Use SIGKILL on the FC pid

fix_steps.action: Or use guest `reboot` with reboot=k boot_args (i8042 reset triggers FC exit)
fix_steps.command: Ensure boot_args contains reboot=k; guest$ reboot

fix_steps.action: Or just SIGKILL from orchestrator

symptom: Guest `reboot` doesn't terminate the Firecracker process. Guest enters reboot loop — kernel restarts but Firecracker keeps running because i8042 reset signal isn't issued.

diagnostic_steps.action: Inspect current boot_args
diagnostic_steps.expected: Should contain 'reboot=k'

diagnostic_steps.action: Confirm guest sees i8042 keyboard controller
diagnostic_steps.expected: i8042 init message present

fix_steps.action: Pre-boot: add reboot=k to boot_args
fix_steps.rollback: Remove reboot=k (reboot loops back to silent stuck state)

symptom: MicroVM boot takes 500+ ms instead of expected ≤125 ms. Serial console is enabled — every kernel printk causes a VM exit.

diagnostic_steps.action: Check boot_args for console=ttyS0
diagnostic_steps.expected: If contains console=ttyS0 → root cause confirmed

diagnostic_steps.action: Measure boot time via boot-timer metric
diagnostic_steps.expected: ≤125 ms when console disabled, multiple-x when enabled

fix_steps.action: Remove console=ttyS0 from boot_args (prod default)
If serial output needed in prod, capture to file via PUT /serial instead of console=ttyS0
fix_steps.validation: Serial output captured without VM-exit overhead

symptom: Guest panics at boot with 'Cannot open root device vda' even though /drives is configured correctly. Guest kernel lacks CONFIG_VIRTIO_BLK.

diagnostic_steps.action: Check guest kernel config for VIRTIO_BLK
diagnostic_steps.expected: CONFIG_VIRTIO_BLK=y

fix_steps.action: Rebuild guest kernel with CONFIG_VIRTIO_BLK=y (and CONFIG_VIRTIO_MMIO=y on aarch64; CONFIG_VIRTIO_PCI=y if --enable-pci)

symptom: x86_64 guest kernel built with CONFIG_ACPI=n fails to enumerate VirtIO devices when Firecracker uses ACPI boot path. Devices appear missing in dmesg.

diagnostic_steps.action: Check guest config
diagnostic_steps.expected: Both =y for ACPI boot path on x86_64

fix_steps.action: Rebuild with CONFIG_ACPI=y and CONFIG_PCI=y
Or fall back to legacy boot: enable CONFIG_VIRTIO_MMIO_CMDLINE_DEVICES=y and CONFIG_X86_MPPARSE=y (note: deprecated)

symptom: Firecracker fails to boot when guest kernel is built for a different architecture than the host (e.g., aarch64 guest on x86_64 host).

diagnostic_steps.action: Check guest kernel vs host arch
diagnostic_steps.expected: Both should be the same (x86-64 or aarch64)

fix_steps.action: Rebuild guest kernel for the host arch
fix_steps.validation: uname -m inside booted guest matches host

fix_steps.action: Or run on a host of the matching arch

symptom: Started Firecracker with --enable-pci but boot_args still contains pci=off. Guest disables PCI scanning and never sees the VirtIO/PCI devices Firecracker exposes.

diagnostic_steps.action: Inspect boot_args and CLI flags
diagnostic_steps.expected: Either remove --enable-pci or remove pci=off — must be consistent

fix_steps.action: Remove pci=off from boot_args when --enable-pci is used
fix_steps.validation: Guest dmesg shows VirtIO PCI devices enumerated
fix_steps.rollback: Drop --enable-pci AND keep pci=off (revert to MMIO transport)

symptom: vCPU thread returns KVM_EXIT_INTERNAL_ERROR. KVM detected an unrecoverable inconsistency (emulation impossible, simul exception delivery, unexpected delivery_event). MicroVM is unsalvageable.

diagnostic_steps.action: Capture suberror code and ndata registers
diagnostic_steps.command: Enable Debug logging; reproduce; grep KVM_EXIT_INTERNAL_ERROR <log>
diagnostic_steps.expected: Suberror enum value (KVM_INTERNAL_ERROR_EMULATION etc.)

diagnostic_steps.action: Check host KVM/microcode versions
diagnostic_steps.expected: Up-to-date per distro security advisories

fix_steps.action: Update host KVM module + CPU microcode + Firecracker version
fix_steps.command: yum/apt update kvm-related packages; load latest microcode; restart hosts

fix_steps.action: If reproducible, file an upstream KVM/Firecracker bug
